title: Fix Lowpoly Mesh Wrong Filled Faces
description: The lowpoly default mesh (Concrete Forest Left, derived from CAD hexagonal-cut-concrete-forest-left) has wrong filled faces — large triangles spanning open space between vertical supports that are not part of the CAD solid. Root cause is likely fill_holes() during CAD→lowpoly regeneration incorrectly capping boundary loops between legs. Fix so the lowpoly mesh is the true mesh of the CAD shape without spurious filled faces.
summary: Fixed wrong filled faces on the default Concrete Forest Left lowpoly mesh. Root cause: CAD→lowpoly regeneration ran fill_holes() on tessellation seams, inventing faces that spanned the open gaps between vertical supports. Rebuilt the mesh from shared BREP face wires instead: BrepkitKernel::solid_face_loops_sync, HalfedgeMesh::from_face_loops (n-gons for simple faces; keyhole triangulation for holes), and orient_faces_consistently for watertight windings. Regenerated concrete-forest-left.mesh.json and default.lowpoly.json to 71 verts / 57 CAD faces with 0 open edges and 0 spanning faces. Added regression tests. Verified: kernel_3d_mesh 24 passed, lowpoly_core --lib 15 passed.
